rule: Phase 2: a double-sign freezes the name, no burn set of keys

breaks.title: A key change filed while unseated can land after the bank is seated again, making its double-sign moot
breaks.scenario: Dynamic mode, a bank V that has a bank of record. V pays its self-stake to another name it owns, so for one block it is not seated. In that block it files a self-service key change K->K2, which its bank of record co-signs. The plan does not say when 'a seated name re-keys only by the 2/3' is checked. If it is checked when the request is carried, like every other request rule, the request is valid. The next block V pays the stake back and is seated again, with the change still pending. At the height where K2 takes effect, V signs two different prevotes (or two proposals) with K. The proof can only land in a later block, where V's current key is already K2. Under the current-key rule it is moot. V double-signed while seated and is never frozen, and its seat changed key without the 2/3. The burn-set design judged evidence against the key recorded for its height, so it would have burned K and frozen V. The current-key rule is what opens this. A 2/3 rotation of a seated bank has the same one-height window, but there the 2/3 chose the rotation.
breaks.fix: Check the seat again when a change falls due, not only when it is filed. A pending self-service key or bank change lapses if its name is in the validator set at that block. Within a block, apply freezes before pending changes. Then only a 2/3 action can make evidence against a seated name moot. No keys are stored.

breaks.title: Nodes stop carrying a proof once the offender leaves the set
breaks.scenario:
Dynamic mode, with today's carry policy unchanged.
1. Bank V queues, for block h, a payment of its self-stake to another of its names (or has its delegators re-delegate).
2. V signs two different prevotes at h.
3. Block h commits with the payment, so V is not in h+1's set.
4. commit deletes V's pending proof (node/node.go:889-894, line 891). slashEvidence would not carry it either (node/node.go:515-527, line 522), and pendingSlashes live only in memory (node/node.go:121).

No block ever carries the proof, so the rule 'freezes the name even if it has left the set' never runs. V is now unseated and unfrozen, so it gets a self-service key change co-signed by its bank of record. Once that lands a day later, any copy someone saved is moot under the current-key rule. V moves its stake back and is seated under the new key. A burn set would not have helped: nothing is carried, so nothing is burned.
breaks.fix: Carry and prune proofs by the validity rule, not by set membership. Keep a pending proof until a committed block carries it, or until the convicted key is no longer the name's current key. That includes a name that left the set or is already frozen, for example one that froze itself right after double-signing, so the 2/3 sees the double-sign before it decides. Optionally, keep pending proofs in the snapshot so a network-wide restart cannot drop them within the change delay.

breaks.title: An unfreeze that keeps the convicted key leaves old evidence live
breaks.scenario: The plan lets the 2/3 name action 'release' a frozen name. Its NewKey is optional and is never compared with the frozen key. Suppose bank V is frozen by proof E, say because a bug made it double-sign. The 2/3 releases V, or re-keys it to a 'new' key that is K again. That happens if an operator re-installs the same HSM key, or if a deterministic key ceremony like eMudhra's reproduces it. K is still V's current key, so E counts again. One dishonest validator puts E into its next proposal, and V is frozen again and leaves the set. This repeats after every release, while E's height is still in the record, and at any time once evidence is judged on the current key (break 4). If K had leaked, the thief also controls V again until then. A burn set would have refused NewKey = K and made a release with the same key impossible.
breaks.fix: Every unfreeze re-keys, as the user put it: 'an unfreeze will pick a new key'. The 2/3 action unfreezes a name only with a NewKey that differs from the key the frozen list holds for that name, and the plan drops 'or releases'. The current-key rule then makes every older proof moot. This needs no new state, because the frozen list already holds that key until the 2/3 acts. If holders' own freezes must keep a plain release, mark evidence freezes with one bit and require the new key only for those.

breaks.title: Judging evidence against the recorded set makes block validity depend on each node's history
breaks.scenario: The signature record is node-local. A validator that joined or re-synced by checkpoint after height h has no validator set for h: fastForward installs only the checkpoint's accounts and its signer set (node/node.go:392-406). Bank V double-signs at h and leaves the set, and honest proposers keep carrying the proof, as the rule asks. Validators that joined since h cannot judge that proof, so they prevote nil on every proposal that carries it. When such a block commits anyway, ApplyBlock fails in commit and they stall until catch-up (node/node.go:875-877). If they hold a third of the power, no proposal carrying the proof can commit, and only rounds proposed by one of them succeed. A dishonest proposer can re-include any still-valid proof to repeat this. The plan also orders the record after the freeze, so when the freeze ships there is no recorded set to judge against. The burn-set design had the same dependence, so a burn set would not have prevented it.

breaks.title: A validator that loses its sign log re-signs the height it was voting in
breaks.scenario:
Bank V's disk dies while height h is open. Alternatively, a power cut corrupts the sign log, Open refuses it (node/persist.go:178-183), and the operator deletes it. V is rebuilt in one of two ways:
- from the backupPath mirror, which copies only the checkpoint (node/persist.go:69-84), while the log lives at SnapshotPath+'.votes' (:131);
- or re-synced from peers, as docs/security.md advises.

With no log, Open goes ahead (persist.go:175-177), and V starts h fresh at round 0 (node/node.go:611-612). Without bootstrap it does that even if the network has moved on. It re-proposes if it is the round-0 proposer, or prevotes nil when the propose timeout fires, which comes before the 3-second catch-up poll. If h is still open, peers hold V's earlier round-0 votes and record the conflict at once. h stays open if V's power was needed for quorum, or if Phase 2's idle chain keeps it open. If the network has moved on, a validator that kept V's old prevote, or the proposer signature the record keeps, can assemble the proof. V is frozen for an outage. In a four-bank network that hands one dishonest bank a veto over every block, and over the 2/3 action that would unfreeze V. A burn set would have burned V's key for good.
breaks.fix: The driver never signs a vote or proposal for a slot where it already holds one signed by its own key, whether from disk or from peers' re-gossip (node/node.go:799-811). After a start without a readable sign log, the node signs nothing until one re-gossip interval and one catch-up poll have passed. The Open error for an unreadable log should say not to delete it. The case where only a dishonest validator kept V's old votes is left to the 2/3 re-key. Mirroring the log to backupPath is not enough, because the mirror is asynchronous and skips commits while busy.

breaks.title: A proposal goes out before its proposer's prevote is on disk
breaks.scenario:
Bank V is the round-0 proposer at height h, and its disk fills, or the filesystem turns read-only after an I/O error.
1. startRound has already queued ActProposal (consensus/driver.go:240) when castVote fails to write the prevote to the sign log and drops it (:314-322).
2. process signs and broadcasts the proposal anyway (node/node.go:732-742). The Phase 1 log keeps a proposal only beside a non-nil precommit (node/persist.go:143-153).
3. The operator frees space and restarts V. Its log has no vote at h, so Start proposes round 0 again from a rebuilt candidate.

The new block differs: the mempool is now empty, and Phase 2 puts the proposer's random value into the signed digest, so it would differ in any case. V has now signed two proposals for (h, 0). Peers still at h record the conflict. Peers past h can pair the new proposal with the proposer signature the record keeps for block h. V is frozen, with the same veto consequence as the lost-log case. A burn set would have burned V's key for good.
breaks.fix: Make a proposal durable before it leaves, as votes are: write its round (or the signed proposal) into the sign log before broadcasting it, and never propose a logged round again after Resume. Alternatively, queue ActProposal only after that round's prevote was cast. Judge 'different proposals' by the signed block digest, never by signature bytes. The node signs its own proposal twice (node/persist.go:146-152 and node/node.go:738), and the two copies are identical only under deterministic signing.

breaks.title: Two pending key changes can put one key under two names
breaks.scenario: An attacker controls names V and N. V files a self-service change to a new key K. Within the delay, N also files a change to K, or registers with K, which applies at once. Each passes 'the new key is already some name's key', because K becomes V's key only when V's change falls due. Both land, and K now serves V and N. When K double-signs as V, only V is frozen: N keeps signing with the convicted key and can be seated later. The 2/3 action's NewKey and genesis (E39) have no uniqueness check at all. A burn set would have retired K under both names. The attacker gains nothing over two separate keys, hence low.
breaks.fix: Count pending new keys as taken. 'Already some name's key' covers current and pending keys, is checked again when a change falls due, and applies to the 2/3 action's NewKey and to genesis. Then each key belongs to exactly one name, and freezing the name retires the key without any burn list.

skeptics.holds:
I tried the following, and the rule survives each one:
- **Forged evidence:** impossible. Both halves must verify under the name's current key, and the network id is bound.
- **Replaying a proof after a 2/3 re-key:** moot under the current-key rule, given break 3's fix.
- **Old votes against a later name that reuses the key:** they cannot be used, provided votes sign the signer's name. Today vote.go signs the signer field.
- **Self-service re-key of a seated name before its proof lands:** blocked, except through break 1.
- **Leaving the set to escape:** fails once nodes carry such proofs (break 2). Every honest proposer carries a proof, so it lands within a block or two, well inside the one-day change delay. The freeze also cancels pending changes.
- **A thief whose stolen key clashes with the bank's votes:** the bank's name is frozen. After the 2/3 re-key, the thief's copy of the key controls nothing. Re-binding it needs the thief to own the target name, and the new key's signature stops it binding someone else's key.
- **Evidence racing a 2/3 name action in the same block:** safe if evidence is judged on the pre-block state and freezes apply before the governance action, as today (ledger/block.go:253-257, :285-288). The plan should state that order. Under the opposite order, a dishonest proposer bundles an old proof with the 2/3 re-key and re-freezes the name under its new, unconvicted key.
- **Two spellings of one name:** the rule holds only if a vote's or proposal's signer field must equal the registered spelling byte for byte. That is the plan's unsettled 'one spelling per name'. Otherwise a validator signs under two spellings, the vote set counts it twice (consensus/voteset.go:59-70 keys votes by the raw string), and Evidence.Valid never pairs the two (consensus/evidence.go:12).
- **Delaying evidence past a window:** gives no escape once validity follows the current key.

**What only a stored key list would stop:** a convicted key coming back later, either under another name, or under the same name after a different key in between. Whoever re-uses it must sign for it, so it mostly harms the re-user. Its one real value is as a tripwire for a deterministic key generator. The immediate case, an unfreeze that keeps the same key, is caught without a list by break 3's fix. So 2 KB per key buys almost nothing.

breaks.title: A mass freeze can empty the validator set or hand it to a small minority
breaks.scenario:
The docs recommend this setup (docs/operating-a-network.md:129-134, docs/security.md:101-105): bank A's always-on machine holds 70% of the power and laptops hold 30%. A double-signs once. The cause can be a release bug, or a disk that confirms fsync and then loses the sign log's last write in a power cut (the log relies on fsync, node/persist.go:92-117). The next proposer carries the evidence. A's name is frozen and leaves the set with its 70%. Then:
(1) The laptops are now the whole set. The chain halts whenever a third of the laptop power is asleep, which the docs say not to rely on.
(2) A laptop that was behind at the freeze block can never catch up by itself. The new commits are signed by laptops holding under 1/3 of its anchor set's power, and verifyCheckpoint needs more than 1/3 (node/node.go:465-475).
(3) Two laptop owners with 21% of the original power now make up the 2/3. One name action re-keys A's name to a key they hold and unfreezes it, and A's 70% of delegated power comes back under their key.
(4) If the bug reaches every bank as each one upgrades, the last banks freeze themselves too, because an honest proposer carries evidence against itself (node/node.go:515-527). The set is then empty: ProposerAt returns "" and Quorum is 1 with no members (consensus/validator.go:63, :77-79). No block and no unfreeze certificate (ledger/reassignment.go:101-111) can ever be valid. Only a re-genesis helps.
Static mode is the worst case because it has no re-delegation. Dynamic mode can re-delegate only while blocks still commit.
Burn set: it would not have helped. The old decision also took a burned key's seat out of the set until the 2/3 reassigned the name (post_emudhra_review_2026-10-27.md:114-116), so the numbers are the same. A burned key could not even be released after the bug was diagnosed.
breaks.fix: Cap what evidence may freeze, using power the state already holds. A double-sign freezes a name only if, afterwards, all frozen names (any cause), counted at their delegated or static power, hold under 1/3 of the seated plus frozen power. Other evidence waits. It stays valid while the key is current, and the case goes to the 2/3 vote. The double-signers that are not yet frozen still sit in that vote, and re-keying them makes their evidence moot. More than 2/3 of the power then always stays seated, so the set is never empty or a minority. A straggler can still verify checkpoints, because the commit signers hold more than 4/9 of its anchor set. Optionally, refuse new delegations to a frozen name so the frozen total cannot be padded. Remaining weakness: under the cap, the proposer picks which evidence lands first. No keys are stored.

breaks.title: Double-signing by a third or more of the power stops the chain before any freeze can land
breaks.scenario:
The review's own C01 setup: three equal static validators, and one key leaks. An eMudhra-style weak key generator would leak many keys at once. The thief signs prevotes and precommits for a junk digest under that key, for every round up to MaxRoundLookahead (consensus/driver.go:13) at the current height, and gossips them. Every honest vote from that key now conflicts with one of these. VoteSet.Add therefore removes the key's power from each round (consensus/voteset.go:59-67). The other two validators hold 2, below the quorum of 3 (consensus/validator.go:63). Even the prevote timeout never starts, because it needs 2/3 of prevotes of any kind (consensus/driver.go:431-435). The height never ends. No block can carry the evidence, the holder's free self-freeze, or a 2/3 name action. The plan's reason for removing frozen names from the set (post_emudhra_review_2026-10-27.md:812-815) assumes a block that never comes. Dynamic mode behaves the same way, so C01's 'dynamic mode self-heals' is true only for a one-off double-sign.
Burn set: it fails the same way, because a burn also needs that block.
breaks.fix: No rule that acts through a block can fix this, so the rule should say so. The freeze covers double-signing by under 1/3 of the power, and a one-off double-sign by more. Persistent double-signing by 1/3 or more, or any leak of 2/3 of the keys, is recovered by a re-genesis from the last committed state. The affected names get new keys and the network gets a new id (E20). The signature record's governance certificates show which 2/3 actions to keep. Write that runbook now, and have docs/security.md warn that with three equal validators, one leaked key ends the chain. Nothing is stored.

breaks.title: A proposal goes out even when the sign log recorded nothing, so an honest restart proposes a second block
breaks.scenario:
Bank P is the round-0 proposer at height h when its disk fills.
- logVote fails (node/persist.go:155-162), so castVote drops P's prevote (consensus/driver.go:317-322).
- startRound has already queued ActProposal (consensus/driver.go:229-241), so process() still signs and broadcasts block B1 (node/node.go:732-742).
- The sign log stores a proposal only together with a non-nil precommit (node/persist.go:143-154).
P cannot log votes, so it cannot vote. If its power is needed, the chain stalls at h, and the operator frees space and restarts P at h. Nothing is logged for h, so startHeight calls Start() (node/node.go:611-613) with a candidate block built from the now-empty mempool (node/node.go:596-607). P signs a different block B2 for (h, 0). Peers already hold B1. With E15 and E16 the pair is valid evidence, so an honest bank is frozen. A remote signer (TODO.md:30, Phase 3) that fails the vote call but answers the proposal call causes the same thing.
Burn set: no help. It would have burned P's key for good.
breaks.fix: Make proposals fail closed like votes (E31). Before sending a proposal, log its slot (height, round) and block hash, and do not send it if the write fails. After a restart, never sign a different block for a logged slot: re-send the logged proposal, or skip proposing in that round if the block is gone. The Phase 3 signer needs a proposal slot next to its vote slots. No keys are stored.

breaks.title: A release without NewKey lets the old evidence freeze the name again, at a moment someone chooses
breaks.scenario:
Bank B holds 25% of the power and double-signs once because of a release bug. The evidence lands and B is frozen. The banks find the bug, and the 2/3 release B with a name action that has no NewKey, because B's key is in an HSM and was never exposed. NewKey is optional (post_emudhra_review_2026-10-27.md:693-697, :784-785). B's key is still its current key and the height is still inside RetainBlocks, so the same evidence is valid again. Any node that kept it includes it in its next block, and B is frozen again. If nodes keep evidence until it is moot, as 'freezes even if the validator has left the set' requires, every honest node does this. A Byzantine holder can instead wait and use it when B's 25% is needed for quorum. On a set near its margin that halts the chain whenever the holder chooses, and each release costs another 2/3 round. Re-keying B back to its old key later brings the evidence back the same way.
Burn set: a burn set would have prevented this one. B's key could never be current again, so the 2/3 had to re-key.
breaks.fix: Make evidence moot once the 2/3 has acted on the name: evidence counts only if its height is above the name's last 2/3 name action. That is one height per name in state, and no key. It also decides the order when a name action and evidence are in the same block. Alternative: mark evidence freezes in the frozen list and require NewKey to lift them.

breaks.title: Judging evidence against the recorded validator set makes block validity depend on what each node kept
breaks.scenario:
Dynamic mode. A double-sign at height h is carried in block h+5. Banks holding 40% of the power joined from checkpoints after h, so they never kept the record for h. They cannot look up the double-signer's seat and key at h, so they reject the block and prevote nil. Today ApplyBlock checks evidence from the evidence alone (ledger/block.go:253-257). The rule adds a lookup in per-node data that is outside the state digest. Because 40% is at least 1/3, the block cannot commit. Every honest proposer that holds the evidence includes it again (pendingSlashes at node/node.go:121, carried by slashEvidence at :515-527). Most rounds then fail, each with a longer timeout, and the double-signer is never frozen. A record served by a dishonest bootstrap peer makes a joining node reject evidence the same way. A node under 1/3 that cannot apply a committed block stops at that height until checkpoint catch-up (node/node.go:875-878).
Burn set: the old design did not have this problem because votes carried the key, so evidence could be checked from its own contents. The problem comes from looking up a past set, not from dropping the burn set.
breaks.fix: Judge evidence against state alone: both votes must verify under the name's current key, which the current-key rule already requires. Drop the lookup of the past set, and keep RetainBlocks as a simple age limit on the evidence height. So that an honest observer cannot convict itself, an honest node should sign no vote at a height where it has no seat. Today every node runs a driver and signs votes (node/node.go:607; castVote has no membership check, consensus/driver.go:314-338). Together with the height rule from the release-without-NewKey finding, a key installed before its name action cannot be convicted for votes it signed earlier. Nothing is stored.

breaks.title: Unfreezing many names takes one 2/3 certificate per name, strictly one after another
breaks.scenario:
A release bug makes 6 of 10 equal banks double-sign. Under the plan all 6 are frozen; with the cap, 3 are frozen and 3 wait. Each unfreeze is its own 2/3 name action. A block holds at most one governance action (ledger/block.go:122-136, :259-261), and each action is bound to the governance sequence (post_emudhra_review_2026-10-27.md:694-695). A node pools only certificates that are complete and valid at the current sequence (node/reassignment.go:37-53), and drops outdated ones (:89-96). So the six cannot be submitted together. Each one is submitted after the previous one lands, and any other 2/3 action in between invalidates every pre-signed one. Recovery takes six rounds of collecting signatures while the chain runs on 40% of its power, and one more outage halts it.
Burn set: the same. It also needed one reassignment per name.
breaks.fix: Let one name action carry a list of (name, NewKey, Bank) entries under one certificate, so a mass recovery is a single 2/3 round. The only keys stored are the new ones.

breaks.title: An unfrozen name rejoins the set at once, under a key its node may not be running yet
breaks.scenario:
Under the plan a frozen bank can hold most of the power (see the mass-freeze finding). The 2/3 unfreeze bank A (70%) with a NewKey at height h. From h+1 the set counts A under the new key. A's node keeps signing with the old key until its operator installs the new one, so A's votes fail the name-to-key lookup. Live power is 30%, below 2/3, and the chain halts until the operator acts. A smaller bank that goes quiet this way can still tip a set that is near its margin.
Burn set: the same gap, because a reassigned name also came back under a new key.
breaks.fix: Give the name back its seat a fixed number of blocks after the name action lands (or at a height the action names), so the node has time to load the key. The action's other effects apply at once. No keys are stored.

skeptics.holds:
Tried, and the rule holds:
- Forging evidence against an honest bank fails: both votes must verify (consensus/evidence.go:11-22).
- A thief who gets its stolen keys frozen never raises its own share. The share always falls, since A/(T-S) < (A+S)/T whenever A+S < T.
- A Byzantine double-signer holding under 1/3 is frozen, and the remaining power, above 2/3, keeps quorum.
- There is no mid-height set change. The set is derived at commit (node/node.go:885), so a freeze takes effect at the next height.
- Honest restarts with a working sign log are safe. Resume restores votes and the lock (consensus/driver.go:173-199), and a proposer never proposes again in a round it voted in (:230). The only gap is the failed-write case in the proposal finding.
- A freeze does not spoil the certificate that would unfreeze others, because votes from non-members are dropped (node/reassignment.go:41, :76-85).
- Evidence older than a 2/3 re-key is moot under the current-key rule. Only the release-without-NewKey case leaks.
- A Byzantine bank holding more than 1/3 can veto any block that carries its own evidence. That is inherent, and the same with a burn set.

Needed, but not breaks:
- Leaving the set as an escape is closed only if nodes keep evidence for unseated names. Today they drop it (node/node.go:515-527, :890-893).
- Static mode needs validatorsFor (node/validators.go:14-19) and the catch-up anchor (node/node.go:465-475) to apply the frozen list.
- Proposal evidence must compare the signed fields, as reportEquivocation already does (node/node.go:711). Otherwise, before E15, someone can swap the block under a genuine signature and frame the proposer.

Inherent to removing frozen names from the set, with or without a burn set: taking an online validator out lowers the online share, since (O-F)/(T-F) < O/T. One freeze can halt a set running near 2/3 until the sleeping validators come back. The docs should say that losing the largest validator must still leave more than 2/3 of the rest online.

Answer to the lens question: with the cap, a one-off mass double-sign (a bug, or fsync that lies after a shared outage) degrades the chain instead of killing it. At most a third of the power leaves, and the 2/3 re-key the rest in batches. Persistent double-signing by 1/3 or more, or a leak of 2/3 of the keys, needs a re-genesis.

Paths are relative to <scratch>/freeze-snapshot.

breaks.title: Evidence validity depends on a node-local, pruned record
breaks.scenario: The rule judges evidence against the (name, key, power) set recorded for its height. State keeps 'nothing else about past pairings' (plan line 817), so only the node-local signature record holds that set, and a node that joins by checkpoint gets none of it: fastForward takes only accounts, the last commit and its signers (node/node.go:392-406). Example: dynamic mode, RetainBlocks set to a month (the plan's sizing). Bank N is admitted at height 1,000,000 and joins by checkpoint. At 1,500,000 a proposer carries evidence of a double-sign at 900,000, which is inside RetainBlocks. Nodes that hold the set for 900,000 accept the block; N cannot judge it. If N rejects it, N prevotes nil whenever a proposer carries it, and honest proposers keep carrying pending evidence (node.go:515-527). Once such nodes pass ⅓ of the power, no block carrying it commits. If they hold less, the block commits, N's commit re-runs ApplyBlock, fails and returns (node.go:875-878), and N stalls until catch-up at every such block. If N falls back to the current state instead, it convicts names the record would spare. One example is a static observer: it signs its own votes with no seat and no sign log (castVote, consensus/driver.go:314-338; cmd/server/config.go:172). Probe: <scratch>/probe-statedet/node/probe_observer_signs_test.go, 1 own vote broadcast. A RetainBlocks cut splits nodes a third way. Whether a height is 'still remembered' depends on the retention in force when it was written (line 719), and state doesn't hold that. The plan also builds the record after the freeze (line 855). A burn set changes none of this: the problem is where the key at height h comes from, not the list.
breaks.fix: Judge evidence only from the pre-block state and the evidence itself. Both halves name one signer and verify under that name's current key. The name governs this block or has held a seat (the Seated bit from the next finding). The name is not already frozen. At most one item per name per block, and its height is at most the block's. The evidence is just the two signed messages, about 7 KB with ML-DSA-65, with no key and no set. Drop the age bound: the plan already says the current-key rule removes maxEvidenceAge's reason (line 855). ApplyBlock then never reads the record, so joining and pruning cannot change validity. Also have the driver sign votes and proposals only when its name is in the set. No keys stored.

breaks.title: A self-service key change moots evidence from heights the name sat in
breaks.scenario: Only a name in the set is barred from self-service changes (plan line 795). A change takes effect a day later (line 779), and from then on evidence counts only against the new key (line 707). Path 1, if the seat is checked only when the request lands: unseated name U requests K1→K2 at block b. Delegations seat U at b+10. The change matures at b+86,400 while U still sits. A double-sign at b+86,399 is moot unless its evidence lands in block b+86,400. Path 2: dynamically admitted bank V signs a conflicting commit for height h and shows it only to a syncing node or a wallet, which is the forgery the record exists to expose. V moves its own stake away in block h+1 and leaves the set, then changes key with its bank of record's co-signature. The forgery surfaces after the change matures but still inside RetainBlocks, so the evidence is moot, and V re-delegates back with K2. The burn-set design as amended caught both paths (new_key_design_review.json, E13 rule): it judged evidence against the key recorded at h and froze the name even after it left. So the escape comes from the current-key rule, not from dropping the list.
breaks.fix: Add one Seated bit per name. ApplyBlock sets it for every name in the set that governs the block, and genesis sets it for static validators. Once the bit is set, the name changes key or bank only by the ⅔ name action. A pending change lapses in the first block its name governs. A once-seated name's key then changes only by a ⅔ re-key, so 'moot after a re-key' means what the plan intends, and self-service requests and evidence never target the same name. One bit per name, no keys.

breaks.title: Nodes drop evidence once the offender leaves the set
breaks.scenario: A pending item is carried only while its offender is a current validator (slashEvidence, node/node.go:519-523), and commit deletes the items of offenders missing from the next set (node.go:889-894). recordLateDoubleSign's comment says the same (:497-500). Bank V signs a re-delegation of its own stake for block h, then double-signs during height h. Block h carries the update, so V is out of the set for h+1, and commit deletes V's evidence as it retires the driver. No block ever carries it, though the plan says leaving must not be an escape. Probe on today's code (dynamic mode, 4 banks): <scratch>/probe-statedet/node/probe_leave_drops_evidence_test.go. Without the re-delegation the evidence stays pending and is carried; with it, the evidence is gone and 0 items are carried. A burn set would not have prevented this. The burn-set prototype pruned only burned keys, but its ledger check accepted evidence only against a current validator (evidenceAdmissible, results/burnset-prototype.patch), so it lost the same evidence.
breaks.fix: Carry a pending item until the committed state shows its name frozen or its key changed, using the same pre-block test as ApplyBlock. Remove the membership filter in slashEvidence and the prune in commit. With the next finding's fix, 'frozen' is a safe point to stop, because every unfreeze retires the key. The burn set's 'already burned' becomes 'already frozen', with no key list.

breaks.title: An unfreeze without a fresh decision and a new key re-arms or erases the evidence
breaks.scenario: NewKey is optional, and the plan keeps 'releases' (lines 694-696, 784-785, 813-814, 825). (a) The ⅔ judge V's double-sign an operator mistake and release V without a new key. K1 is still current, so any validator that kept the evidence carries it again and V is frozen in the next block, after every release. (b) The banks collected a bank change or a key rotation for V before it double-signed. The action binds only (name, sequence) (line 695), so it lands after the freeze. If any name action unfreezes, it lifts the freeze though nobody weighed the double-sign, and a bank-only action leaves K1 current, so (a) follows. (c) V double-signs and self-freezes in the same block. Nodes drop the evidence because V is already frozen. V asks the ⅔ to release a false alarm and is back on K1 with the evidence gone. A burn set prevented (a) and (c): a burned K1 could never vote again, so releasing without a new key was pointless, and re-carried evidence was inadmissible. It did not prevent (b) when the action was a rotation.
breaks.fix: A name action lifts a freeze only if its signed fields carry an explicit Unfreeze, and Unfreeze requires NewKey. A rotation or bank-change certificate without it never unfreezes. Every unfreeze retires the key the evidence verifies under, so the current-key rule makes all older evidence moot. This matches 'an unfreeze picks a new key' and adds nothing to state. If a holder's false-alarm self-freeze must stay releasable without a new key, add a one-bit cause to the frozen entry and require NewKey only for a double-sign freeze.

breaks.title: Proposal evidence freezes an honest proposer after a failed log write
breaks.scenario: The sign log writes only votes; a proposal reaches disk only together with a precommit of its value (logVote, node/persist.go:137-163). The proposer's driver returns ActProposal before it casts its prevote (startRound, consensus/driver.go:230-244). process then signs and sends the proposal whatever happened to that prevote (node/node.go:732-742). If the prevote's log write fails (a full disk; the log fails closed), the proposal is already out with nothing on disk. The operator frees space and restarts. The log has no vote for that round, so the node proposes the round again from a rebuilt mempool. In Phase 2 the digest also carries a fresh random value, so the block always differs. Probe on today's code: <scratch>/probe-statedet/node/probe_proposal_log_test.go. A sole validator with its sign-log directory missing sent the proposal 7 times and 0 votes. After the directory was restored and the node restarted with another payment, it signed a second, different proposal for height 1 round 0. With proposal evidence, an honest bank is frozen and leaves the set with its delegated power. A burn set would not have prevented it; it would have burned the honest key for good.
breaks.fix: Write the signed proposal to the sign log before sending it, failing closed as for a vote. After a restart, re-send the logged proposal for that round instead of building a new one. Count only two different blocks for one (height, round) as a conflict. Resume restores validRound from the highest precommit only (driver.go:173-199), so an honest re-proposal of the same block can carry a different ValidRound. No keys.

breaks.title: Certificates kept for life can't be checked without their signers' keys
breaks.scenario: This is the one per-key record still needed. The record keeps reassignment and parameter certificates for life, but the validator set only for RetainBlocks heights (plan lines 712-716). Votes name their signer, so checking an old signature needs that name's key at the certificate's height. Example: bank D sat with a key from its self-service registration, which is not kept, and the ⅔ later re-keyed it; the kept action holds only the new key. After RetainBlocks, D's signature on a kept seizure certificate can't be checked. A node can then serve a forged certificate for that sequence, and no honest node can refute it by signature. The evidence that froze a name is not kept at all, though lines 719-720 say the ⅔ 'cannot vote away the record of their own double-signs'. A burn set would not have helped: it lists convicted keys, not signers.
breaks.fix: Keep for life each (name, key) pair that ever held a seat, written when the name first governs a block and whenever the ⅔ re-key it, and keep each item of evidence a block carried. That is a few KB per bank key, kept so old signatures stay checkable, not a growing list of burned keys.

skeptics.holds: Forgery fails: evidence needs two signatures by the name's own key, so no proposer can freeze an honest name. Reading the current key from the pre-block state makes re-conviction after a ⅔ re-key moot. A ⅔ re-key and evidence in the same block hold if ApplyBlock applies the evidence before the governance action, as block.go:283-288 already orders slashes before reassignments. The reverse order would refreeze a name the ⅔ just re-keyed, using evidence the rule calls moot. A self-freeze and evidence in one block both freeze, which is harmless. A freeze cancels a pending change, including one maturing in the same block, as long as freezes apply before changes take effect. Old keys are not a risk. After a ⅔ re-key the old key belongs to no name. Its holder may bind it to a new name, but the old votes name the old signer, so they convict nothing (the signer's name must be in the signed fields). A burned-key list would stop nothing, since keys are free to generate. A frozen name's key stays listed, so the 'new key is already some name's key' check keeps it unusable while frozen. Confiscation is weak: today's applySlashes zeroes the balance (block.go:100-103), but the offender can pay everything out before the evidence lands, so the freeze is the real penalty, which supports 'simply freezes'. With the fixes, ledger state holds no key beyond each name's current one, plus one Seated bit per name. Nothing needs a burned-key list. The probes ran in a separate copy of the tree; no snapshot file was changed.

synthesis.verdict:
The core idea holds. Freezing the name instead of keeping a list of burned keys loses nothing that matters, because every message names its signer and the current-key rule makes old proofs moot once the ⅔ re-keys the name. The only cases a key list would still catch are a convicted key bound again later, under another name or under the same name after a different key, and those harm only whoever binds it again.

As written, though, the rule does not hold, for three reasons:
- Judging evidence against each node's own pruned record of past validator sets makes nodes disagree on whether a block is valid, and the plan ships that record after the freeze.
- Freezing a third or more of the power hands the chain to a minority, or can empty the validator set for good.
- Five smaller gaps let a double-signer escape, or get an honest bank frozen.

The seven changes below close these. None stores a key or adds ledger state; the only format addition is an Unfreeze flag on the ⅔ name action.

required_changes.why:
The past (name, key, power) sets exist only in each node's own signature record (plan lines 704 and 712-716). State keeps 'nothing else about past pairings' (816-817).

The record differs between nodes:
- A node that joined or re-synced from a checkpoint has none of it (fastForward, node/node.go:392-406).
- A copy served by a bootstrap peer cannot be checked against state.
- A RetainBlocks cut applies only to new records (line 719), so whether a height is still remembered is not a function of state.

So nodes disagree on block validity. Nodes that cannot judge a carried proof prevote nil. If they hold a third of the power, no block carrying the proof commits. If they hold less, ApplyBlock fails in commit and they stall until catch-up (node/node.go:875-878). The plan also ships the record after the freeze (line 855), so at first there is nothing to judge against.

The current-key rule already fixes which key to use, so the lookup adds only membership, and the driver rule covers that. Today every node runs a driver (node/node.go:607), and castVote signs without checking membership (consensus/driver.go:314-338). I re-ran <scratch>/probe-statedet/node/probe_observer_signs_test.go: a static observer broadcast its own vote. Observers need no sign log (cmd/server/config.go:172), so without the driver rule a merchant node's restart could freeze its name.

A dishonest key holder gains nothing, because the free self-freeze already lets it freeze its own name.

Code paths are relative to <scratch>/freeze-snapshot. Plan lines are in review/post_emudhra_review_2026-10-27.md there.

Evidence against a third or more of the power can land only if those signers vote for the block that carries it. Honest nodes prevote any valid block, and slashEvidence carries evidence even against the proposer itself (node/node.go:515-527). So an honest but faulty bank freezes itself, while a dishonest third simply vetoes its own evidence. The cap therefore gives up no deterrence.

The docs recommend one always-on bank holding more than ⅔ (docs/operating-a-network.md:129-134, docs/security.md:101-105). Without the cap, one honest fault in that bank removes 70% of the power. The fault could be a release bug, or a disk that loses a synced write in a shared power cut. Then:
- the laptops become the whole set;
- a node that was behind never catches up, because new commits carry under a third of its anchor set's power (verifyCheckpoint, node/node.go:465-475);
- 21% of the original power becomes the new ⅔, enough to re-key the frozen bank's name to a key it holds and take back that bank's 70%.

A bug that hits every bank freezes all of them, because each proposer carries evidence against itself. The set is then empty: ProposerAt returns an empty name, and Quorum is 1 with no members (consensus/validator.go:63, :78-79). No block and no unfreeze certificate can ever be valid again.

With the cap, more than ⅔ of the power stays seated. The remaining set's ⅔ is over 4/9 of the original, which is above the one-third fault bound. Nodes that fell behind can still verify checkpoints. The burn set had the same exposure.

required_changes.change:
Every unfreeze re-keys. A ⅔ name action lifts a freeze only if:
- its signed fields say Unfreeze;
- it carries a NewKey different from the key the frozen list holds for that name.

Drop 'or releases' (plan lines 784-785, 813-814, 825). A frozen name's listed key changes only through that Unfreeze. An action signed without Unfreeze never lifts a freeze.
required_changes.why:
NewKey is optional (line 694), and a release keeps the convicted key current, so the same proof becomes valid again. Any node that kept it freezes the name again in its next block. A dishonest node can hold the proof back and use it when the name's power is needed for quorum.

The action binds only the name and the governance sequence (line 695), and an evidence freeze does not advance the sequence. So a key-rotation certificate the banks signed before the double-sign stays valid, and it would lift a freeze nobody voted on. A bank that double-signs and freezes itself in the same block could also come back on its convicted key as a 'false alarm'.

This change matches 'an unfreeze will pick a new key' and adds no state, since the frozen list already holds the key. Combined with the current-key rule, it makes every older proof moot. It keeps the burn set's one real benefit: the old key is refused.

The plan says evidence 'freezes the name even if the validator has left the set since' (lines 704-706), but today's code drops it.

I re-ran <scratch>/probe-statedet/node/probe_leave_drops_evidence_test.go on the snapshot code (dynamic mode, four banks). In the bad case, a bank double-signs at height h and a re-delegation of its stake lands in block h. Commit then deletes the proof, and no block carries it. Without the re-delegation, the proof is kept and carried.

The bank, now unseated and unfrozen, can file a self-service key change. Once that lands a day later, any saved copy of the proof is moot. With the filter removed, honest proposers land the proof within a block or two, well inside that day. The burn set had the same gap.

'A name in the validator set changes key or bank only by the ⅔ name action' (line 795) is listed among the request rules, which are checked when a request is filed. In dynamic mode a bank can get around it:
1. It pays its self-stake to another of its names, so it is unseated for one block.
2. In that block it files a key change, co-signed by its bank of record.
3. The next block it pays the stake back.
4. A day later the change lands while the bank is seated, so its seat changes key without the ⅔.

A double-sign at that height is signed with the old key. Its proof can only land once the new key is current, so the current-key rule makes it moot. A ⅔ rotation of a seated name keeps the same one-height window, but there the ⅔ chose it.

Separately, the check 'the new key is already some name's key' (line 797) ignores pending keys. A registration, which applies at once, or a second pending change can therefore put one key under two names. Freezing one name then leaves the convicted key working under the other.

Without the stated order, a change maturing in the same block as a freeze could replace the convicted key in the frozen list. A later Unfreeze could then pick that key again.

required_changes.change:
Make a proposal durable before it is sent. The proposer sends its proposal only after its prevote for that round is in the sign log (or it logs the proposal first). If the write fails, nothing is sent, as with votes (E31). After a restart, the node never signs a different block for a round it has logged.

Proposal evidence is two proposals for the same height and round whose signed block hashes differ. A different ValidRound, or different signature bytes, never count. E15 must land first.
required_changes.why:
startRound queues the proposal before the prevote is cast (consensus/driver.go:229-244). process signs and broadcasts the proposal whatever happened to the prevote (node/node.go:732-742). The sign log keeps a proposal only alongside a non-nil precommit (node/persist.go:143-153).

So if the prevote's write fails, because the disk is full or the filesystem has gone read-only, the proposal is already out with nothing on disk. When the operator frees space and restarts the node, it proposes the same round again from a rebuilt mempool. Phase 2's random value in the signed digest makes that block differ every time.

I re-ran <scratch>/probe-statedet/node/probe_proposal_log_test.go and it confirmed this: an honest single validator signed two different proposals for height 1, round 0. With E16, that pair freezes an honest bank.

Resume restores validRound only from the highest precommit (consensus/driver.go:173-199). An honest re-send of the same block can therefore carry a different ValidRound, which is why only blocks should be compared.

required_changes.change:
Handle a start without the sign log.

At minimum, the docs and Open's error message for an unreadable log say:
- never delete the sign log;
- never restart a validator from a backup at the height it was voting in.

Better, in a few lines of code:
- the driver never signs a vote or proposal for a slot where it already holds one signed with its own name, whether from its log or from peers' re-gossip;
- a validator that starts with a snapshot but no log for that height signs nothing until one re-gossip interval has passed.
required_changes.why:
The given premise covers restarts with an intact log. Two cases fall outside it: a dead disk, or an unreadable log (Open refuses it, node/persist.go:178-183) that an operator then deletes.

In both cases the node comes back without its log. Either it is restored from the backup mirror, which copies only the checkpoint (node/persist.go:69-84; the log is at SnapshotPath+'.votes', :131), or it re-syncs. Open goes ahead with no log (:174-177), and the node starts the open height afresh (node/node.go:611-612). It proposes again, or prevotes nil when the propose timeout fires, which is the same interval as re-gossip.

Even when its old vote arrives by re-gossip, the driver counts it but does not mark that slot as sent, so castVote signs the conflicting vote anyway. Peers holding the old vote then freeze an honest bank. In a four-bank set that leaves three, and one dishonest bank can then veto every block, including the unfreeze.

Severity is low because this needs a lost or deleted log, and the ⅔ re-key recovers it.

rejected.title: Double-signing by a third or more of the power stops the chain before any freeze can land (liveness lens)
rejected.reason: This is true, but it is not a flaw in this rule. An equivocator holding a third or more is un-counted every round (consensus/voteset.go:59-67). The rest stay below quorum, and not even the prevote timeout starts (consensus/driver.go:432). No remedy that acts through a block can respond, and the burn set could not either; the case is outside the one-third fault bound. Its fix is documentation plus a re-genesis runbook, which is folded into the scope statement of the second change.

rejected.title: Unfreezing many names takes one ⅔ certificate per name, one after another (liveness lens)
rejected.reason:
The mechanics are correct:
- a block carries one governance action (ledger/block.go:122-136, :259-261);
- certificates are bound to the sequence and pooled only while currently valid (node/reassignment.go:37-53, :89-96).

But this is a matter of recovery speed, not a hole in the rule. Serial ⅔ votes are the owner's model for rare cases. With the cap, more than ⅔ of the power stays seated meanwhile, so nothing halts. A batched name action can come later if mass recovery ever matters.

rejected.title: An unfrozen name rejoins the set under a key its node may not be running yet (liveness lens)
rejected.reason: The name action carries the new key's own signature, so the key's holder has it before the action lands. A frozen name is out of the set and, under the first change, signs nothing, so its node can switch keys while still frozen. Switching keys exactly at a ⅔ rotation of a seated name is a node feature unrelated to the double-sign rule.

rejected.title: A self-service key change makes moot a forged commit shown only to a syncing node or wallet (state lens, path 2)
rejected.reason: Path 1 is merged into the fifth change. Path 2 needs a conflicting commit certificate. That means more than ⅔ of the power signing a forgery, or a third or more forking. Such a group can re-key itself by ⅔ or veto its own evidence whatever the rule says. A single bank that double-signs and then leaves the set is frozen within a block or two under the fourth change, far inside the one-day delay.

rejected.title: Certificates kept for life can't be checked without their signers' keys (state lens)
rejected.reason: Out of scope for this rule. It concerns the governance certificates the signature record keeps for life, and after the first change the freeze never reads the record. Its fix keeps every seat key for life, which belongs in the record's own review. Its point that the record keeps no evidence is owner question 4.

rejected.title: Fixes not taken: a per-name Seated bit, a per-name height of the last name action, and a membership test based on the Seated bit

owner_questions: The one-third cap (second change): do you accept that evidence never freezes a double-signer holding a third of the power or more, alone or together with names already frozen, and that this case goes to the ⅔ vote or a re-genesis? If the freeze stays unconditional, as the plan has it now, one honest fault in a bank above ⅔ (the setup the docs recommend) leaves the chain to a minority: 21% of the original power can re-key that bank's name to itself. A correlated bug can also empty the set for good.

Evidence age (first change): with the record out of the rule, should a proof count for as long as its key is current? That matches 'the key is burned' and needs the least code. The alternative is a plain age limit set by a ledger parameter. It limits how long a dishonest node that alone holds a proof can keep it and choose when to freeze the name.

Should the signature record keep each proof a block carried? Each is about 7 KB with ML-DSA-65, and proofs are rare. This would let the ⅔ and later auditors see why a name was frozen. As planned, the record keeps commit certificates, proposer signatures and set changes but no evidence. So the claim that the ⅔ 'cannot vote away the record of their own double-signs' (plan lines 719-720) does not cover evidence freezes.
Lost sign log (seventh change): do you want the small driver guard? Or are the docs rule and the ⅔ re-key enough for a validator that loses its disk partway through a height?
